name: Sarcosine (N-methylglycine)
short: Small schizophrenia trials reported good tolerability with no significant side effects. A case report describes hypomania when sarcosine was added to an antidepressant and an antipsychotic.
text: A meta-analysis of six randomised trials (234 adults with schizophrenia) of sarcosine added to antipsychotic medication, all using 2 g per day, described the compound as having good tolerability, and a 6-week placebo-controlled trial in 38 patients reported that sarcosine was well tolerated with no significant side effect noted. These trials were small and short. On the other side, a case report describes a 34-year-old woman with schizophrenia taking olanzapine and the antidepressant venlafaxine who developed hypomania (reduced need for sleep, elevated mood and activity) after about ten weeks of added sarcosine; it settled after her venlafaxine dose was lowered. The authors called it the second case report of important mood changes when sarcosine was added to antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment.
